name: AUDIT | SSO for Entra ID
description:
During a TSM engagement we had a customer get confused when setting up attributes through SSO.  They made the mistake of using different names between the 2 systems causing the values to not be mapped.  

The guide for Understand and Configure Domo Single Sign-On Using SAML (https://domo-support.domo.com/s/article/360042934374?language=en_US) has the following note:

When defining which attributes get passed to Domo, use the following names for each of the attributes. (All attribute names should be lowercase except for SAML_SUBJECT. The "email" attribute is required; all others are optional.)

This note is missing on a many of the SSO specific guides and can cause a little confusion with users when setting up attributes.  It would be nice to have the below note added to the Azure SSO with one small change to cover the naming conventions.  Can this note be added to the attribution mapping part of the Azure SSO guide (https://domo-support.domo.com/s/article/360043438033?language=en_US)? 

Suggested Note:
When defining which attributes get passed to Domo, use the following names for each of the attributes. (All attribute names should be lowercase except for SAML_SUBJECT.  The Domo Attribute Key value should match the SSO providers attribute name to map the values properly.  The "email" attribute is required; all others are optional.)

name: CRITICAL for Large Datasets
description:
"CRITICAL for Large Datasets (300K+ rows): Always map the Optional group by field when using slicer cards with large datasets. Without this mapping, the card downloads and processes ALL rows even if only a few unique values exist, causing severe performance issues and unresponsive dashboards. Map the same column from 'Items' (or appropriate dimension) to Optional group by to aggregate data before processing.
Example: A 'Brand' slicer with 10 unique values in a 334K row dataset will process only 10 values instead of 334K rows when Optional group by is used."
Pointed out by Engineering during DOMO-473323 (Jan 2026). This best practice resolved critical performance issues that nearly jeopardized a customer POC. Should be prominently highlighted to prevent similar issues.

name: Manage Cloud Integrations
description:
In our cloud amplifier help article, we describe what the following grants do 

Override Default Cloud
Manage Cloud Integrations

Based on my testing, our help article has the description backwards.

Current Help Article:
Manage Cloud Accounts — Allows a user to add/remove cloud accounts and add/remove tables from a cloud account. This grant also allows a user to change the default storage cloud.

Note: This grant must be assigned to a user with the Manage DataSet grant to work properly.

Override Default Cloud — Allows a user to use any storage cloud account that is shared with them instead of the default cloud. If you do not have this grant, you can't use any other cloud besides the default cloud.

Note: This grant must be assigned to a user with the Edit DataSet or Manage DataSet grant to work properly.


How it actually works:
Based on my testing, when a user is assigned 'Override Default Cloud' they can now switch the admin default cloud in More > Admin > Features > Cloud Integration, but they do not have access to change which integration a new datasets uses.

When the user is given 'Manage Cloud Accounts, ' they do not have access to change the default in the admin section, but they do have the ability to change the integration used on a new dataset. The user can select Domo or any other integration they have been granted permission to.


Tested internally with this dataset and user

DS:
https://domo-support-prod5.domo.com/datasources/ccf3c2d9-83fa-4f47-a8e2-aff02c011053/details/overview

User:
https://domo-support-prod5.domo.com/admin/people/889852397?tab=profile

name: Update "Credentials Pane"
description:
Update this section:

"Credentials Pane
This pane contains fields for entering credentials to connect to your Domo developer account as well as your Google Sheet. The following table describes what is needed for each field:  

Field
Description

Service Token JSON

Paste the JSON Service Token you generated in Step 3: Creating a Service Account, in the "Prerequisites," above."

I've seen several people get stuck on this part of the connector setup because they are trying to paste ONLY the Key section of the file Service Token file, instead of the ENTIRE file. The file is formatted like this:
{
  "type": "service_account",
  "project_id": "projectid",
  "private_key_id": "projectkeyid",
  "private_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----xxx-----END PRIVATE KEY-----",
  "client_email": "domo-google-sheets@domo.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "client_id": "clientid",
  "auth_uri": "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth",
  "token_uri": "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token",
  "auth_provider_x509_cert_url": "https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v1/certs",

  "universe_domain": "googleapis.com"
}

Often customers are just copying and pasting this:
-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----xxx-----END PRIVATE KEY-----

instead of the entire contents. We should just let the customer know they need to paste the entire file contents.

name: Update misc. Beast Modes text
description:
Can we update the note that says "Calculations you create using Beast Mode are inherited when you drill from one view to another using the same DataSet. However, calculations are not inherited when you drill to a different DataSet"?
When you drill down and change the parent dataset there are two beastmodes instead of one and often share the same name since there is one for each dataset.  Many customers think that since the beast modes are "not inherited" there should only be one and it causes a lot of confusion and pushback.  
Engineering says "When making a drill card it needs to reference the beast modes from the parent card, so technically these aren't duplicate beast modes. One is used on the parent card and one is used on the drill card with a reference back to the parent card's beast mode that is available for use on the drill card. It's recommend to not reuse names for beast modes from the parent card to help prevent confusion".

name: Upsert in WB 5.1
description:
Add below as FAQ
" What will break an Upsert dataset?

The following will cause an Upsert dataset to Reindex:
- Deleting data versions from the dataset history (note: this is NOT the same as deleting records from an Upsert dataset; simply deleting records, for example using the CLI, does NOT require reindexing)
- Changing column data types
- Changing the Primary/Upsert key (adding OR removing columns from the primary/upsert key)
- Re-adding columns that were previously deleted
- Adding or removing columns won't usually cause a re-index, but it may, depending on what optimizations have been automatically put in place on the dataset."

Reference dojo post:
https://community-forums.domo.com/internal/discussion/57905/what-will-break-an-upsert-dataset#latest

name: Workbench pull files - IK
description:
Is there a way for Workbench to pull files based on a "contains" in the filename rather than the exact file name?

Instead of setting up a job (Configure, Source, Edit) with a file name at the end of the source edit path:
- Create a new directory to store the incoming file
- In the Workbench job setup (Configure tab)—>Source, Edit » Path to directory (with no filename)
- Set up the rest of the job normally and save

Whenever a file appears in your created directory, the WB will upload that file(and any other files that are in the directory).

Caution:
-The files that land in the directory MUST have IDENTICAL schema as the file uploaded before the new file.
- Need to build in Windows logic to delete the file after it is uploaded (maybe in Windows Task Scheduler), as only one file should reside in the directory at a time. For example, if you had two files in the directory and a third file appeared in the directory (all files having identical schemas), the workbench would upload all three files, which is why there can only be one file in the created directory at a time.

Reference dojo post:
https://community-forums.domo.com/internal/discussion/57976/workbench-and-filename-contains#latest

name: Cloud Amplifier (Integration) DataSets sect. update
description:
The KB Article for Cloud Amplifier Datasets (https://domo-support.domo.com/minasan/s/article/4412849158167?language=en_US) has a section with a table that shows what cloud amplifier datasets are compatible with. 

In this table, there are bright green checkboxes for dataset views, indicating that cloud amplifier datasets are compatible with dataset views. 

This is only partially true, as you can create a view from a colud amp dataset and join it to another colud amp dataset from the same colud connection. However, we need to call out what cloud amplifiers can NOT do with dataset views, specifically, joining a cloud amp dataset to a dataset from domo and/or another cloud connection. 

Here are datasets which this can be tested and verified against:

My Snowflake Cloud Amp Dataset: https://domo-support-prod1.domo.com/datasources/76bd19d2-f219-4bde-803b-68881dfa8950/details/overview
My Standard DSV: https://domo-support-prod1.domo.com/datasources/082c86bd-0d1c-4837-8e71-553eb8c93c2f/details/overview
My SQL DSV: https://domo-support-prod1.domo.com/datasources/140103b0-5284-4e4b-a93e-869dff431bfe/details/data-lineage

See screenshots for the results of the following 4 tests, along with what our KB article currently shows. 

Test 1 - Joining Cloud Amp Dataset to Standard view with Standard View
Test 2 - Joining Cloud Amp Dataset to SQL view with Standard view
Test 3 - Joining Cloud Amp Dataset to Standard view with SQL View
